newsitem.title: USA: Osmonics optimistic for 1997, sees costs.
newsitem.headline: Osmonics optimistic for 1997, sees costs.

text.p: Osmonics Inc, which makes purification and filtration systems, said Tuesday it is optimistic for 1997 results but sees earnings for the year trimmed a bit due to costs associated with conversion to a new management information system.

Osmonics said it expects to see savings in 1997 as the system becomes fully operational. Once the system is in place, the company said it should be able to handle annual sales transactions of more than $1 billion with minimal upgrades.
The system provides real-time inventory and order processing at all of the company's business units worldwide.
For the 1996 year, Osmonics said the conversion had cost about $0.05 a share in earnings, with nearly $0.03 of that in the fourth quarter.

Osmonics reported 1996 fourth quarter earnings equal to $0.24 a share, flat with profits earned in the same period in 1995. Sales rose to $40.7 million from about $36 million in the 1995 fourth quarter.
Other income was up significantly in the 1996 fourth quarter compared with a year earlier due to sale of some investments that had appreciated, Osmonics said.
The tax rate for 1996 rose to 32.4 percent from 29.4 percent in 1995.
"As we end a strong year and look forward to 1997, we continue to be optimistic," said D. Dean Spatz, chairman, in a statement.
"Backlogs are up and our streamlined sales organization is making good inroads with many excellent partners," he said.
Shares of Osmonics were trading off 1/4 to 21.
